walkthroughs.body_html:
Approaches in Psychology — a core area of A-Level Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Approaches in Psychology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Approaches in Psychology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the behaviourist view on the nature-nurture debate?
options: Both nature and nurture equally.
Strongly nurture - we are shaped by environmental conditioning.
Strongly nature - behaviours are innate.
Picking participants who match the population profile.
Strongly nature - behaviours are innate.
Picking participants who match the population profile.
Just grabbing whoever is around (any haphazard method).
Every member of the target population has an equal chance of selection.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Bottom-up profiling”?
options: Imprisonment aims to deter, rehabilitate, incapacitate and protect; UK recidivism around 48% within one year.
Sutherland (1939): criminal behaviour learned from associates whose pro-crime attitudes outweigh anti-crime ones.
Canter's UK approach: statistical analysis of crime scene data to derive profiles; investigative psychology.
Criminals score high on extraversion, neuroticism and psychoticism (E, N, P); inherited nervous system underactivity.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Custodial sentencing”?
options: Imprisonment aims to deter, rehabilitate, incapacitate and protect; UK recidivism around 48% within one year.
Sutherland (1939): criminal behaviour learned from associates whose pro-crime attitudes outweigh anti-crime ones.
FBI approach (Ressler 1986): classify crime scene as organised or disorganised to infer offender characteristics.
Criminals score high on extraversion, neuroticism and psychoticism (E, N, P); inherited nervous system underactivity.
